title: Staggered warmup priority hotpatch for multi-variant fanout latency wave
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted API and several Dedicated tenants) reported intermittent first-token latency waves and sustained tokens/sec degradation during high fanout requests across mixed-model endpoints. Symptoms included TTFT spikes to 1.8–3x baseline for 10–30s windows, tokens/sec collapse on multiplexed paths, and model variant divergence (quantized variants slower than float32).

Scope: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (reported from two enterprise VPCs). Affects large-context workloads and chat-style sessions that fan out across model-variants (default + quantized fallback).

Initial hypothesis: scheduler affinity and warmup sequencing create a staggered-start effect where large-context requests stall on kernel selection / KV prefetch serialization, while background GC and async weight streaming preempts the fast-path kernels. This leads to a brief period of priority inversion that starves first-token workers and collapses throughput for multiplexed sessions.

Immediate mitigation applied: 1) Introduced a hotpatch to bump high-priority first-token lanes (TTFT-critical) to real-time scheduling on serving nodes for 30m windows while we validate. 2) Added a short-circuit that disables async weight streaming for models in affected clusters to avoid preemption spikes. 3) Deployed a circuit-breaker that prevents simultaneous KV prefetch for >8 high-cost requests per worker to reduce serialization pressure.

Business impact: Multiple enterprise customers experienced user-facing latency regressions that triggered escalations. Temporary mitigation restored baseline TTFT within 8–12 minutes of rollout in hosted clusters; Dedicated and Private require coordinated customer approvals for the hotpatch.

Next steps: 1) Complete root-cause analysis (kernel selection heuristics vs GC timing) and instrument more granular tracing. 2) Land targeted scheduler fix that enforces first-token affinity without resorting to global real-time scheduling. 3) Add unit/integration tests to cover concurrent KV prefetch scenarios. 4) Plan staggered rollout across Dedicated and Private with customer sign-off and rollback plan.
